rationale: Both experience cases show a parent prediction contradicted despite a supported intermediate diagnostic claim. U-P: plan_length>=1 was supported (1.0>=1.0) yet total_successes>=2 failed (observed 0); the earliest executed failure was operator_syntax at index 0 with executed_actions=0, not the plan_length metric the parent fix targeted. U-S: mean_residual<0.003 was supported yet NMSE decrease>=0.002 failed (observed 0.0005); the rationale substituted a bin-level association (high-|v| RMSE) for the population NMSE target. Ordering rationale: (1) R03 first -- both cases rewrote task-specific assumptions (plan reconstruction walk; adding a v-amplitude term) that risked altering the environment definition rather than the artifact; preserving explicit task rules prevents the next agent from repeating this drift. (2) R04 second -- U-S directly substituted a per-bin mean_residual for the population NMSE metric and bin identity for candidate identity; U-P's success metric (total_successes) was conflated with plan_length. Exact metric/unit/scope discipline must precede diagnostic reasoning. (3) R02 third (U-P) -- the earliest observed execution signal was at action index 0 with operator_syntax errors; the parent fix targeted plan_length which is a proposed metric, not the observed failure. Future agents should anchor on the first executed failure, not the most recently edited line. (4) R06 fourth (U-S) -- the U-S rationale treated a marginal high-|v| bin RMSE association as a necessary mechanism (amplitude-dependent damping) without considering alternatives; a supported association is a hypothesis, not a proof. The two cases together do not evidence R01 (input-format failure), R05 (source-location tracing), R07 (forecast threshold), or R08 (scope-creep) as the dominant failure mode, so the prior S0 ordering on those is not retained. Each rule is anchored to a specific observed failure in the supplied cases.
